name: Colorado
tagline: Fourteeners, gold camps, the San Luis Valley and the Santa Fe Trail's prairie ruts.
intro: Colorado's byways climb over the high passes of the San Juans and the Front Range, follow the Arkansas and the upper Rio Grande through old mining towns, and run out across the eastern plains along the Santa Fe and Overland trails. This chapter follows the 26 Colorado Scenic and Historic Byways, a program begun in 1989 and run by the Colorado Department of Transportation with the Colorado Scenic and Historic Byways Commission. Thirteen of them also carry national designation, more than in any other state, and several double as National Forest Scenic Byways or BLM Back Country Byways; new nominations are currently on hold.

members.name: Alpine Loop
members.blurb: Old ore-wagon roads cross the San Juans over Cinnamon and Engineer passes, both above 12,000 feet, passing seven ghost towns on the way. It takes a high-clearance four-wheel-drive vehicle and closes for the winter.

members.name: Cache la Poudre - North Park
members.blurb: CO 14 climbs from Fort Collins up the canyon of the Cache la Poudre, the state's only Wild and Scenic River, over 10,276-foot Cameron Pass and down into North Park around Walden, where moose and antelope are ordinary sights.

members.name: Collegiate Peaks
members.blurb: The road follows the Arkansas River below the Sawatch Range through Buena Vista and Salida, with side roads up to the old mining camps of St. Elmo and Winfield and to Mount Antero, where aquamarine is dug.

members.name: Colorado River Headwaters
members.blurb: The Colorado starts here as a clear stream through meadows and red rock gorges. The byway follows it from Grand Lake, an old resort on the state's largest natural lake, and ends on gravel through Upper Gore Canyon.

members.name: Dinosaur Diamond
members.blurb: The Colorado side of a two-state loop runs from Fruita and Grand Junction north to Rangely and Dinosaur National Monument, past the Dinosaur Journey Museum and the Canyon Pintado historic district.

members.name: Flat Tops Trail
members.blurb: A back road between Meeker and Yampa crosses the old White River Plateau timber reserve, by the turnoff to Trappers Lake, the so-called Cradle of Wilderness, through working ranch and timber country. Winter closes it at Dunkley Pass.

members.name: Frontier Pathways
members.blurb: From Pueblo the road climbs into the San Isabel National Forest and down to Westcliffe and Silver Cliff, a dark-sky community in the Wet Mountain Valley, on an old frontier corridor where the Ute traveled long before Spanish explorers.

members.name: Gold Belt Tour
members.blurb: Phantom Canyon Road follows an old gold-ore railroad grade through granite tunnels, and the 1892 Shelf Road hangs 200 feet above its creek, both linking the mining towns of Cripple Creek and Victor with Cañon City and Florence.

members.name: Grand Mesa
members.blurb: CO 65 leaves I-70 up the canyon of Plateau Creek and climbs into spruce forest 11,000 feet up on the Grand Mesa, past Land's End Overlook and some of its more than 300 trout lakes, before dropping to Cedaredge.

members.name: Guanella Pass
members.blurb: A 22-mile pass road from Georgetown climbs through aspen and spruce along cascading creeks to beaver meadows and tundra above timberline, under Mount Bierstadt. In winter it closes at Naylor Lake and Burning Bear Campground.

members.name: Highway of Legends
members.blurb: CO 12 climbs west from Trinidad beneath the Spanish Peaks and the red rock fins of the Dakota Wall to Cuchara Pass, and a partly gravel extension crosses 11,248-foot Cordova Pass from Aguilar.

members.name: Lariat Loop
members.blurb: A 40-mile loop in the foothills west of Denver joins Golden with Morrison and Evergreen, climbing Lookout Mountain on the five-mile Lariat Trail to Buffalo Bill's grave and passing Red Rocks and Dinosaur Ridge.

members.name: Los Caminos Antiguos
members.blurb: Across the broad San Luis Valley, the road runs from the Great Sand Dunes past Fort Garland to San Luis, the oldest surviving town in Colorado, and on to Conejos, home of the state's oldest parish.

members.name: Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans)
members.blurb: From Idaho Springs the road climbs more than 7,000 feet in 28 miles to 14,130 feet, into alpine country of mountain goats, pikas and cold lakes. The summit road opens in summer by reservation only.

members.name: Pawnee Pioneer Trails
members.blurb: Highways and dusty county roads cross the shortgrass prairie of the Pawnee National Grassland to the Pawnee Buttes, through pronghorn and prairie dog country and past railroad towns that sprang up and then declined.

members.name: Peak to Peak
members.blurb: Colorado's oldest scenic road, laid out in 1918, runs 55 miles along the Front Range from Estes Park toward Black Hawk, facing the Continental Divide, with gravel spurs to the Moffat Tunnel portal and the ghost town of Apex.

members.name: San Juan Skyway
members.blurb: A 236-mile loop through the San Juans ties Durango to Telluride, Ouray and Silverton, with the Million Dollar Highway between the last two, and passes the cliff-dwelling country of Mesa Verde National Park.

members.name: Santa Fe Trail
members.blurb: The byway follows 188 miles of the old trade route up the Arkansas River to Bent's Old Fort, a trading post turned historic site, then cuts southwest to Trinidad and Raton Pass. Wagon ruts still show in the prairie.

members.name: Silver Thread
members.blurb: CO 149 shadows the upper Rio Grande between the old mining camps of Creede and Lake City, past North Clear Creek Falls and the Slumgullion earth slide, then runs on north to Blue Mesa Reservoir.

members.name: South Platte River Trail
members.blurb: The shortest byway in the state is a 19-mile loop from Julesburg, with markers at the four Julesburg townsites, Colorado's only Pony Express home station and the site of Fort Sedgwick, built in 1864.

members.name: Top of the Rockies
members.blurb: From Leadville, at 10,200 feet the highest incorporated town in the country, the road crosses the Continental Divide three times, under Mount Elbert and Mount Massive, and climbs over Independence Pass to Aspen.

members.name: Tracks Across Borders
members.blurb: Between Durango and Chama, New Mexico, the road follows the history of the Denver and Rio Grande narrow gauge, through Ignacio, home of the Southern Ute Indian Tribe, past Navajo Lake and up a spur to Chimney Rock.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Trail of the Ancients
members.blurb: Gravel and paved roads around Cortez cross the dry canyon country of the Ancestral Puebloans to Hovenweep and Yucca House, past the restored McElmo Creek Flume, with a branch to the Four Corners.

members.name: Trail Ridge Road: Rocky Mountain National Park
members.blurb: US 34 crosses Rocky Mountain National Park between Estes Park and Grand Lake, climbing to 12,183 feet on open tundra where wildflowers bloom in midsummer and elk cross the meadows. Closed in winter.
members.note: Shown on the map as Trail Ridge Road/Beaver Meadow Road.

members.name: Unaweep/Tabeguache
members.blurb: CO 141 runs through Unaweep Canyon, cut into the Uncompahgre Plateau down to Precambrian rock, then follows the Dolores and San Miguel rivers past the old Hanging Flume and the uranium country around Uravan.

members.name: West Elk Loop
members.blurb: A 205-mile loop from Carbondale passes the old coke ovens at Redstone and the ranch towns of Paonia and Crawford near the Black Canyon of the Gunnison, then returns by Crested Butte over the gravel of Kebler Pass.
